decisions.choice: swore an oath (nishba): the root of Shibah
decisions.reason: The verb "swear" comes from the same root as the number seven (sheva) and as the name the well receives the same day (verse 33).

source.text: וַיְהִ֣י׀בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא וַיָּבֹ֨אוּ֙ עַבְדֵ֣י יִצְחָ֔ק וַיַּגִּ֣דוּ ל֔וֹ עַל־אֹד֥וֹת הַבְּאֵ֖ר אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָפָ֑רוּ וַיֹּ֥אמְרוּ ל֖וֹ מָצָ֥אנוּ מָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was on that day, and came [the] servants of Isaac and told him about the well that they had dug, and said to him, we have found water.

en.L: And on that same day Isaac's servants came and told him about the well they had dug, and said to him, "We have found water."
en.B: That same day Isaac's servants came to report on the well they had been digging. "We have struck water!" they told him.
en.R: That same day Isaac's servants came and told him about the well they had been digging. They said, "We have found water!"

es.L: Y aconteció aquel mismo día que vinieron los esclavos de Isaac y le informaron acerca del pozo que habían cavado, y le dijeron: «Hemos hallado agua».
es.B: Ese mismo día llegaron los siervos de Isaac para darle noticias del pozo que estaban cavando. «¡Encontramos agua!», le dijeron.
es.R: Ese mismo día, los siervos de Isaac vinieron a contarle del pozo que estaban cavando. Le dijeron: «¡Hemos encontrado agua!».

fr.L: Et ce même jour, les esclaves d’Isaac vinrent et l’informèrent au sujet du puits qu’ils avaient creusé, et ils lui dirent : « Nous avons trouvé de l’eau. »
fr.B: Ce même jour, les serviteurs d’Isaac vinrent lui rendre compte du puits qu’ils creusaient. « Nous avons atteint l’eau ! » lui dirent-ils.
fr.R: Le même jour, les serviteurs d’Isaac sont venus lui parler du puits qu’ils étaient en train de creuser. Ils lui ont dit : « Nous avons trouvé de l’eau ! »

sw.L: Ikawa siku ile ile watumwa wa Isaka wakaja, wakamweleza habari za kisima walichokuwa wamechimba, wakamwambia, "Tumepata maji."
sw.B: Siku ile ile watumishi wa Isaka walikuja kumpa habari za kisima walichokuwa wakichimba. "Tumefikia maji!" wakamwambia.
sw.R: Siku ile ile watumishi wa Isaka walikuja, wakamweleza habari za kisima walichokuwa wakichimba. Wakasema, "Tumepata maji!"

decisions.choice: servants
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable (style guide); Literal keeps "slave".

source.text: וַיִּקְרָ֥א אֹתָ֖הּ שִׁבְעָ֑ה עַל־כֵּ֤ן שֵׁם־הָעִיר֙ בְּאֵ֣ר שֶׁ֔בַע עַ֖ד הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And he called it Shibah; therefore [the] name of the city [is] Beersheba until this day.

en.L: And he called it Shibah; therefore the name of the city is Beersheba to this day.
en.B: He named it Shibah, "Oath", and that is why the town is called Beersheba to this day.
en.R: Isaac named the well Shibah, which means "oath." That is why the town there is still called Beersheba, which means "well of the oath."

es.L: Y lo llamó Sibá; por eso el nombre de la ciudad es Beerseba hasta el día de hoy.
es.B: Lo llamó Sibá, «Juramento», y por eso la ciudad se llama Beerseba hasta hoy.
es.R: Isaac llamó al pozo Sibá, que quiere decir «juramento». Por eso el pueblo que está allí todavía se llama Beerseba, que quiere decir «pozo del juramento».

fr.L: Et il l’appela Shiba ; c’est pourquoi le nom de la ville est Beer-Shéba jusqu’à ce jour.
fr.B: Il l’appela Shiba, « Serment », et c’est pour cela que la ville s’appelle Beer-Shéba aujourd’hui encore.
fr.R: Isaac a appelé le puits Shiba, ce qui veut dire « serment ». C’est pour cela que la ville qui est là s’appelle toujours Beer-Shéba, ce qui veut dire « puits du serment ».

sw.L: Akakiita Shiba; kwa hiyo jina la mji ni Beer-sheba hata leo.
sw.B: Akakiita Shiba, "Kiapo", na ndiyo sababu mji huo unaitwa Beer-sheba mpaka leo.
sw.R: Isaka akakiita kisima hicho Shiba, maana yake "kiapo." Ndiyo sababu mji ulioko huko bado unaitwa Beer-sheba, maana yake "kisima cha kiapo."

decisions.choice: Shibah ... Beersheba: "oath" ... "well of the oath"
decisions.reason: Shibah sounds like the words for oath and for seven. Abraham had already named the place Beersheba after his oath with Abimelech and the seven lambs (21:28-31). Isaac's new well and new oath renew the name, as he renewed his father's well names (verse 18).

decisions.choice: "Oath" (B); which means "oath" ... "well of the oath" (R)
decisions.reason: The meanings are given so the reader can see why the name fits (m1).

decisions.choice: "Shiba" for the well's name
decisions.reason: The name is transcribed from the Hebrew as in the other languages. In Swahili "shiba" is also the verb "be full, satisfied", an accidental echo a reader may notice; "Sheba" would avoid it but blurs the name with the second half of "Beer-sheba". A reviewer may prefer another form.

source.text: וַיְהִ֤י עֵשָׂו֙ בֶּן־אַרְבָּעִ֣ים שָׁנָ֔ה וַיִּקַּ֤ח אִשָּׁה֙ אֶת־יְהוּדִ֔ית בַּת־בְּאֵרִ֖י הַֽחִתִּ֑י וְאֶת־בָּ֣שְׂמַ֔ת בַּת־אֵילֹ֖ן הַֽחִתִּֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And was Esau a son of forty years, and he took [as] wife Judith, daughter of Beeri the Hittite, and Basemath, daughter of Elon the Hittite.

en.L: And Esau was forty years old, and he took as wife Judith the daughter of Beeri the Hittite, and Basemath the daughter of Elon the Hittite.
en.B: At forty, Esau took two wives, both of them Hittites: Judith, daughter of Beeri, and Basemath, daughter of Elon.
en.R: When Esau was forty years old, he married two Hittite women. One was Judith, the daughter of Beeri. The other was Basemath, the daughter of Elon.

es.L: Y tenía Esaú cuarenta años, y tomó por mujer a Judit, hija de Beerí el hitita, y a Basemat, hija de Elón el hitita.
es.B: A los cuarenta años, Esaú tomó dos esposas, ambas hititas: Judit, hija de Beerí, y Basemat, hija de Elón.
es.R: Cuando Esaú tenía cuarenta años, se casó con dos mujeres hititas. Una era Judit, hija de Beerí. La otra era Basemat, hija de Elón.

fr.L: Et Ésaü était âgé de quarante ans, et il prit pour femme Judith, fille de Béeri le Hittite, et Basmath, fille d’Élôn le Hittite.
fr.B: À quarante ans, Ésaü prit deux femmes, toutes deux hittites : Judith, fille de Béeri, et Basmath, fille d’Élôn.
fr.R: Quand Ésaü a eu quarante ans, il a épousé deux femmes hittites. L’une était Judith, la fille de Béeri. L’autre était Basmath, la fille d’Élôn.

sw.L: Esau alikuwa mwenye umri wa miaka arobaini, akamwoa Yudithi binti Beeri Mhiti, na Basemathi binti Eloni Mhiti.
sw.B: Esau alipokuwa na miaka arobaini alioa wake wawili, wote wawili Wahiti: Yudithi binti Beeri, na Basemathi binti Eloni.
sw.R: Esau alipokuwa na umri wa miaka arobaini, alioa wanawake wawili Wahiti. Mmoja alikuwa Yudithi, binti wa Beeri. Mwingine alikuwa Basemathi, binti wa Eloni.

decisions.choice: forty years old: the age at which Isaac married
decisions.reason: Isaac married Rebekah at forty (25:20). Abraham had taken great care that Isaac's wife should not be a Canaanite (24:3); Esau marries two.

decisions.choice: Judith and Basemath: names given differently in 36:2-3
decisions.reason: The list of Esau's wives in 36:2-3 names Adah daughter of Elon the Hittite, Oholibamah, and Basemath daughter of Ishmael (called Mahalath in 28:9). The two lists come from different records, and women sometimes bore more than one name; the Hebrew of each passage is followed as it stands.

source.text: וַתִּהְיֶ֖יןָ מֹ֣רַת ר֑וּחַ לְיִצְחָ֖ק וּלְרִבְקָֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And they were bitterness of spirit to Isaac and to Rebekah.

en.L: And they were a bitterness of spirit to Isaac and to Rebekah.
en.B: These wives made life bitter for Isaac and Rebekah.
en.R: Esau's wives made Isaac and Rebekah very unhappy.

es.L: Y ellas fueron amargura de espíritu para Isaac y para Rebeca.
es.B: Estas esposas le amargaron la vida a Isaac y a Rebeca.
es.R: Las esposas de Esaú hicieron muy infelices a Isaac y a Rebeca.

fr.L: Et elles furent une amertume d’esprit pour Isaac et pour Rébecca.
fr.B: Ces femmes remplirent d’amertume la vie d’Isaac et de Rébecca.
fr.R: Les femmes d’Ésaü ont rendu Isaac et Rébecca très malheureux.

sw.L: Nao wakawa uchungu wa roho kwa Isaka na kwa Rebeka.
sw.B: Wake hao waliyafanya maisha ya Isaka na Rebeka kuwa machungu.
sw.R: Wake wa Esau waliwahuzunisha sana Isaka na Rebeka.

decisions.choice: bitterness of spirit: deep grief
decisions.reason: The phrase means lasting grief and vexation. It prepares for Rebekah's words in 27:46 and for Jacob being sent to find a wife among their own people (28:1-2).
